claim.summary: The single-pair shifted squared-modulus dominance theorem lifts to a finite list of real-coordinate competitors. If each competitor satisfies the pairwise residual bound, or if a shared scalar B bounds every residual and lies below every shift gap, then every listed competitor has strictly smaller shifted squared modulus.
claim.single_pair_identity: shiftedSqMod c a b - shiftedSqMod c u v = 2*c*(a-u)+((a^2+b^2)-(u^2+v^2))
claim.finite_list_conclusion: forall p in competitors, shiftedSqMod c p.1 p.2 < shiftedSqMod c a b
claim.shared_bound_condition: forall p in competitors, residual(p) <= B and B < 2*c*(a-p.1)
claim.shared_bound_conclusion: forall p in competitors, shiftedSqMod c p.1 p.2 < shiftedSqMod c a b

proves: finite-list lift from a shared residual envelope B
does_not_prove: actual spectrum extraction from a matrix
existence of a maximum over a matrix spectrum
strict spectral-abscissa hypothesis for a matrix eigenvalue
that a strict-abscissa eigenvalue of a real matrix is real
